QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_31

question.text: A donor — Shubham Family Trust — is the engaging party, and Antyodaya Seva Sangh is the SE being assessed under SAS 1000. The Trust has requested the SIA team to also provide fundraising advisory services to Antyodaya for the next year. How should the SIA respond?

answer.text: Accept, since the advisory fee will be paid by the donor, not the SE
Decline the combined mandate — providing advisory services to the SE while acting as its independent SIA would compromise independence and create a self-review threat
Accept and disclose the combined mandate in the AIR
Accept the advisory work only after the SIA engagement is signed off — restart the independence clock

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 5.2(e) Independence and Section 5.9 ethical framework require the SIA to be 'independent of the activity being audited wherever practicable, and should in all cases act in a manner that is free from bias and conflict of interest'. Dual mandates (advisory + assurance on the same SE) create self-review and advocacy threats that cannot be safeguarded adequately. **The Trap:** A ignores that the beneficiary of the combined service is the SE, not the donor. C (disclosure) cannot cure a structural independence breach. D (delayed restart) doesn't remove the ongoing self-review — the advisor would be auditing their own advice one cycle later. **Cross-Exam Context:** NISM III-A / III-C (compliance) and X-A / X-B (IA) have analogous self-review prohibitions; XXIII reinforces it for SIA work. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** In your firm, maintain a 'prohibited services' list covering fundraising advisory, strategy consulting, program design, and outcome-indicator selection for any SE you assess — declining cleanly is cheaper than defending an ICAI SIAB disciplinary case.
